passage:
In the school library, Ms Kaur noticed Payal sitting alone again, far from Vandana's table. Six months ago the two had been inseparable.
When Payal's phone buzzed, she flinched, read it and typed a reply fast. "Sorry, sorry," she whispered to no one.
Ms Kaur sat down beside her. "You've seemed worried lately. Want to talk?"
Payal hesitated, then it came out in pieces. Yuvraj didn't like Vandana. He got upset if Payal replied late, so she'd stopped going to Vandana's house. She felt guilty whenever she laughed with anyone else. "I keep saying sorry for things I didn't do," she said. "Maybe it's my fault."
"It's not your fault," Ms Kaur said quietly. "Caring about someone shouldn't make your world smaller. Thank you for telling me." She stayed with Payal until the bell, then walked her to the school counsellor's room that same afternoon, and Payal agreed to talk there.

qa.q: Why had Payal stopped going to Vandana's house?
qa.a: Yuvraj got upset if Payal replied late, so she stopped going to Vandana's house.

qa.q: What does Payal's constant 'sorry' suggest about how she feels?
qa.a: It suggests Payal feels guilty for innocent things and is tiptoeing to avoid upsetting Yuvraj, even blaming herself.

qa.q: How did Ms Kaur respond in a wise way?
qa.a: Ms Kaur listened calmly, told Payal it wasn't her fault, stayed with her and took her to the school counsellor the same afternoon.

qa.q: What might Vandana be experiencing as Payal pulls away?
qa.a: Vandana may feel confused and hurt, losing a close friend without understanding why, and might even think Vandana did something wrong.

grounding: Shows a teenage girl feeling guilty for innocent things and dropping a friend to keep her boyfriend calm, and a teacher bringing in a trusted adult's view.

passage:
Dear Harsha didi,
I'm writing because I can't say this on the family group, and Mummy would panic.
You know Nakul. He's sweet, mostly. But lately I feel like I'm always in trouble without doing anything. If I don't reply in five minutes, he asks who I was with. When I went to Tanya's birthday, he didn't talk to me for two days, so I skipped the next party. I've stopped going to dance class because it finishes late and he gets "worried".
The strange part is that I feel guilty all the time, as if I'm the one who's wrong. I keep making myself smaller so he stays calm.
Is this normal? You're the only grown-up I trust not to laugh or shout. Could you call me on Sunday?
Love,
your little sister, Gargi

qa.q: Why has Gargi stopped going to dance class?
qa.a: Gargi stopped because it finishes late and Nakul gets 'worried'.

qa.q: Why does Gargi feel guilty even though she hasn't done anything wrong?
qa.a: Nakul's reactions have made Gargi feel always in trouble, so she blames herself and keeps shrinking her life to keep him calm.

qa.q: How could Harsha respond when calling Gargi on Sunday?
qa.a: Harsha could listen calmly, tell Gargi it isn't her fault, and on that call help her bring in a parent or school counsellor the same day, rather than waiting to see.

qa.q: How might Nakul see his own 'worry'?
qa.a: Nakul probably sees his worry as care, not realising it is making Gargi drop friends and dance to keep him calm.

grounding: Illustrates a teenage girl's strain in a controlling relationship, feeling guilty and giving up friends and dance, and reaching out to a trusted older cousin.
